(def ^:private find-and-cache-best-method
  (fn [name dispatch-val h method-table prefer-table default-dispatch-val]
    (let [fmt (fn [v] (if (nil? v) "null" (str v)))
          best-entry (loop [entries (seq method-table) be nil]
                       (if entries
                         (let [e (first entries)
                               k (key e)]
                           (if (isa? h dispatch-val k)
                             (let [be (if (or (nil? be) (dominates h k (key be) prefer-table)) e be)]
                               (when-not (dominates h (key be) k prefer-table)
                                 (throw (suss.bootstrap/error
                                          (str "Multiple methods in multimethod '" name
                                               "' match dispatch value: " (fmt dispatch-val) " -> " (fmt k)
                                               " and " (fmt (key be)) ", and neither is preferred"))))
                               (recur (next entries) be))
                             (recur (next entries) be)))
                         be))]
      (if (nil? best-entry)
        (get method-table default-dispatch-val)
        (val best-entry)))))
rationale: Expand the complete pinned defn to def/fn, retaining its documentation (#30). Follows Clojure's MultiFn.findAndCacheBestMethod: it walks the method table in its seq order (a hash map, as in Clojure), keeps the dominating entry and throws when neither dominates, and falls back to the default method. It takes the tables' values and returns the method; -get-method writes the cache, since the tables are MultiFn's mutable fields. Messages are Clojure's, with each dispatch value formatted as String.format's %s formats it: with str, and "null" for nil.
